summary: The evidence does not support any incident during the 06:05–15:05 UTC shift. (1) Transfers: only one outbound transfer was over 5 MB. It moved 21.8 MB from records to 10.20.0.45:873 (stor-nas-01, the approved backup NAS) at 11:46 (ev_f2c7ce0f5524). That is consistent with policy. (2) The records-app access.log on the host is missing 183 lines that the collector kept. All of them come before the 08:48:04 rotation, and policy archives the rotated part off the host, so retention explains the absence. All other forwarded logs match the collector. The workstation auth.log rotation at 08:48 left its .1 copy on the host. (3) The workstation heartbeat stopped for 210 s (11:54:52–11:58:22) and its counter reset. One local auth line never reached the collector. The host holds more than the collector, so this is not log removal, but the cause is unknown. A skeptic review kept all three findings. Attribution: no account is tied to any incident, and no human operator was established.
open_questions: What caused the workstation heartbeat gap and counter reset at 11:54–11:58 (forwarder or host restart, or a network problem)?
Was the 11:46 rsync to stor-nas-01 the scheduled backup? Flow records don't show the contents.
File-metadata snapshots and shell histories were reviewed only through the transfer check, not searched directly for staged files.
